explanation: A lexical pole that fires on the token of particular words whatever their part of speech: words for an arrangement, a specification or its price, i.e. script, schedule, plan, budget, bid/bidding, request(s), policy, list, cost, price, timer, signal, strategy, and also want/need (about 0.35-0.75 of max, even as verbs: 'They will script it' is as strong as 'the script'), plus multi-digit or decimal numerals (486, 378, 1.089, about 0.4-0.7) and the concessives ' despite'/' Despite'/'regardless of' (about 0.4-0.85). Text without any of these words stays near or below 0.25 of max: pronouns, function words, adjectives, everyday verbs (make, take, see, love, said, went), spelled-out or single-digit numbers, and people, household and nature nouns (man, mother, child, door, window, cat, water, river, house, book). Generic object nouns (dog, car, bread, sky, project) sit around 0.2-0.4 and may just cross the line.
